name: Homo/Phobic

tenures.role: tag team — PTC Tag Team Tournament finalists; the first PTC Tag Team Champions
tenures.source: The PTC "New Era" I-PPV's own card, Superstars, Pre-Show and results pages (promotions/ptc/archive/new-era-2003-*.html)
tenures.note: Dated from the tournament rather than from a roster page: the event's own front page puts the tournament at six months old on 20 April 2003, and the results' own commentary and Shane Stone's opening promo both put it at eight — either way the pairing was competing through 2002.

caption: Shane Stone and the Bum Boozler's own pairing, which came through a PTC Tag Team Tournament its own commentary called eight months long to win the final at New Era in April 2003 and become the alliance's first Tag Team Champions.
notes: The team name is recorded exactly as the fed's own card, Superstars, Pre-Show and results pages billed it. The billing itself differs between those pages: "Homo/Phobic (EWA/UWF)" on the card, both men filed under the UWF alone on the Superstars page. The pairing appears nowhere in the surviving record outside the PTC Tag Team Tournament and this event; both men's own continuing runs are recorded on their own entities.

name: Unholy Matrimony

tenures.role: tag team — PTC Tag Team Champions, won on the judges' scores for the three-way "Purgatory with a Pinata" match of April 2005 that no federation hosted and nobody ever wrote; the belts went to the Killer Pirates from the Outer Caribbean the following month when the pair no-showed the defence
tenures.source: PTC's own forum (accession 0160), the alliance's own boards: "Tag Team Division Sign ups: March" (post 139843, topic 12956), 14 Mar 2005 — the team's own sign-up; "Tag Team Title Match" (post 142892, topic 13360), 1 Apr 2005 — the match's own announcement; "PTC Tag Team Titles Match Roleplaying" (posts 144529 and 144903, topic 13478), 11-12 Apr 2005 — the card and the pair's own roleplay "Nightlife"; "PTC Tag Title Match" (post 147097, topic 13686), 26 Apr 2005 — the judges' scores and the title ruling; "PTC Tag Title Match" (posts 148625 and 149811, topic 13774) and "Tag Open Challenge?" (post 150691, topic 13767), 6-22 May 2005 — the defence against the Killer Pirates from the Outer Caribbean; "PTC Title Histories (Back to PIT)" (post 170694, topic 15747), 27 Oct 2005 — the alliance's own title lineage; and "Top Ten Matches Your Character Was In" (post 199384, topic 17963), 30 May 2006 — the Killer Pirates' own account of how the reign ended. Corroborated outside the board by PTC's own encyclopedia (promotions/ptc/archive/ptcpedia-seymour-almasy.html and -2008.html) and by PRIME's own roleplay "The Nobody Puts Up His Dukes, Part III" of 11 May 2005 (promotions/prime-2003/rp/the-nobody-puts-up-his-dukes-part-iii-et-match-overkill-2005-05-11.html).
tenures.note: The team's whole life, from the board's own posts. They signed up for the alliance's March 2005 tag division as "Unholy Matrimony", billed from the UWF, the sign-up naming them "The Final Fantasy" Seymour Almasy and "The One Winged Angel" Aerith Almasy, and were put straight into a three-way for the PTC Tag Team Championship: "Six Kendo Sticks. Three tag teams. Two gold belts. One pinata. Zaro chance of anyone leaving with their dignity intact. This is... Purgatory with a Pinata~!", against the champions, billed Los Muchos Macho Mascadas (White Tiger and Pajaro de Presa, also of the UWF), and Soul Purpose (Noah Hanson and Fury, of WMW). One roleplay each was the limit. NO MATCH WAS EVER WRITTEN: no federation offered to host it after weeks of asking, and the championship changed hands on the judges' scores alone — two of the three judges placed Unholy Matrimony first and the third named only a second and a third place, and the ruling, posted 26 April 2005, reads "Sean is the new Tag Team Champion defeating the others." THE REIGN ENDED WITHOUT A MATCH OF ITS OWN EITHER: the Killer Pirates from the Outer Caribbean were booked against them through May 2005, and the Pirates' own side wrote a year later, listing his best matches, "PTC Tag Team Championship - Killer Pirates vs. Unholy Matrimony. Despite the no show by my opponents, I won the PTC Tag Team Championship belts". The alliance's own title history, posted 27 October 2005, places them sixth in the PTC Tag Team Championship's order, between the Masked Monkeys (Pajaro de Presa and White Tiger) and the Killer Pirates, and records the championship itself as discontinued and retired. THE REIGN IS RECORDED with the championship's other reigns, from 26 April 2005, the day of the ruling, to 28 May 2005, when the Killer Pirates took the belts uncontested: the history post gives an order and no dates — "I don't have dates. I just have orders of champions" — and both dates are PTC's own title log's, the first also the ruling post's. FOUR MENTIONS THAT ARE NOT THIS TEAM, checked and carrying no edge: Global Championship Wrestling's own roleplay "The Wheels Go 'Round 'n 'Round" of 1 October 2008 uses "that unholy matrimony" as the ordinary English phrase, for a wished-for combination of one wrestler's old ring skills with his current blood lust, and names neither member; so do FAW's "The Best Ideas are Often the Simplest" (16 October 2002, a stench), NAPW's "Phenoms Return" (April 2014, a suburban marriage) and a PTC roleplay of 9 January 2007 ("Lets make unholy matrimony with the belt on the line").

tenures.role: tag team — UWF World Tag Team Champions
tenures.source: The UWF's own Sunday Afternoon Supremacy cards: 16 November 2003 (promotions/uwf/archive/sas-2003-11-16.html, "And NEW Tag Team Champions: SEYMOUR ALMASY & AERITH HEARTILLY") and 14 December 2003 (promotions/uwf/archive/sas-2003-12-14.html); the title's own history dates the reign 16 November to 14 December 2003 (titles/uwf-world-tag-team.html).
tenures.note: The UWF's cards field the pair as World Tag Team Champions under their own names, Seymour Almasy and Aerith Heartilly, not under the team name. They won the titles on 16 November 2003 and lost them to the British Blazers on 14 December 2003.

identity.note: CARE RECORD (both members are Sean Simon Williams' characters, on the memorial register; dedication-level handling). The decorated-aka guard reads this name against the registry's bare "Unholy" entities. Recorded as a separate team from unholy-cswa (CSWA) and unholy-dwo (the DWO): unrelated promotions, no shared member, and nothing in any of the three records connecting them. The overlap is the ordinary English phrase this team's own roleplay plays on, and says out loud: "It...is sort of sacrilegious, isn't it."

caption: Seymour Almasy and Aerith Heartilly's divorced-couple tag team, a pairing that had held the UWF World Tag Team Championship for four weeks in 2003 before it took the name and, in April 2005, the PTC Tag Team Championship on the judges' scores for a three-way pinata match no federation ever hosted — champions no longer a month later, when they no-showed the Killer Pirates of the Outer Caribbean.
notes: The name is Seymour Almasy's own invention and the pair's own roleplay stages him coining it — "do you like the name I came up with for us?" — with Aerith reading it back: "It...is sort of sacrilegious, isn't it. We're divorced, and yet we can't keep our hands off of each other. We love each other, and yet we remain in lust. Our lives are lived in physicality, both carnal with one another, and violent in competition." That roleplay, "Nightlife" of 12 April 2005, is the team's only surviving text of its own, and it is written by the same hand as both characters: it was posted from the memorial subject's own account on the board, the account already on his memorial row. It dates their teaming earlier than the name — Almasy calls her "the best tag team partner I've ever had" and recalls her pinning to win them the UWF World Tag Team Championship, the reign both their own records already carry (16 November - 14 December 2003) — and it gives her a submission of her own, the Cactuar Crossface, and a spell in XUDF before she came back. The pairing is billed from the UWF throughout, but no held UWF document bills them under this team name.

name: Soul Purpose

tenures.role: tag team — WMW's pair in PTC's March 2005 tag division: winners of the contenders' roleplay over the Killer Clowns from Outer Space, then second in the three-way for the PTC Tag Team Championship
tenures.source: PTC forum, E-Wrestling: "Tag Team Division Sign ups: March" (post 138187, topic 12956), 1 Mar 2005 — the team's own sign-up; "Tag Team Title Contenders Announced!" (post 138477, topic 12983), 3 Mar 2005; "PTC Tag Team Titles Match Roleplaying" (posts 144529 and 145116, topic 13478), 11-14 Apr 2005; "PTC Tag Title Match" (post 147097, topic 13686), 26 Apr 2005 — the judges' placings.

caption: Noah Hanson and Fury, Wrestling Midwest's tag team in PTC's March 2005 division, who won the contenders' roleplay over the Killer Clowns from Outer Space and finished second to Unholy Matrimony in the three-way for the PTC Tag Team Championship.
notes: Signed up on 1 March 2005 as Soul Purpose, billed from WMW, with Noah Hanson and Fury as its two members. The contenders' roleplay against the Killer Clowns from Outer Space (LOW) was announced as theirs on 3 March 2005, earning the match against the champions. The April title match was a three-way of Soul Purpose, Unholy Matrimony and the Masked Monkeys, which no federation hosted; the ruling post of 26 April 2005 places the team second. The first tenure date is the sign-up post; the contenders' roleplay itself came earlier.
